//==
// # Spatial structures
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Uniform grids and space-filling curve codes
//  - Implicit surfaces
//  - Kd-trees
//  - Overlap, intersection, and culling
//  - Proximity queries
//  - Ray and sweep queries
//  - Bounding volume hierarchies and region trees

//==
// # Uniform grids and space-filling curve codes
//
// Flat, non-hierarchical spatial indexes keyed by cell coordinate — sparse hash
// grids and dense binning grids, both storing their buckets in CSR form — plus
// the Morton (Z-order) codes that linearize a cell coordinate into a single
// sortable integer.

//==
// ## Hash and binning grids

// A sparse uniform grid over the plane, keyed by integer cell coordinate
// (world position divided by CellSize, floored). Only occupied cells are
// stored: cell i has coordinate CellCoordinates[i] and items
// ItemIndices[BucketOffsets[i] .. BucketOffsets[i+1]) (half-open CSR;
// BucketOffsets has one more entry than CellCoordinates).
type SpatialHashGrid2D
    implements IValue, ISpatialIndex2D
{
    CellSize: Number;
    CellCoordinates: Array<IntegerVector2>;
    BucketOffsets: Array<Integer>;
    ItemIndices: Array<ItemIndex>;
}

// A sparse uniform grid over space, keyed by integer cell coordinate. Same
// CSR encoding as SpatialHashGrid2D with 3D cell coordinates.
type SpatialHashGrid3D
    implements IValue, ISpatialIndex3D
{
    CellSize: Number;
    CellCoordinates: Array<IntegerVector3>;
    BucketOffsets: Array<Integer>;
    ItemIndices: Array<ItemIndex>;
}

// A dense uniform binning grid over a bounded 2D region: every cell has a
// bucket. Cells linearize row-major with X varying fastest: cell (i, j) is
// bucket j * CellCounts.Width + i. Bucket b's items are
// ItemIndices[BucketOffsets[b] .. BucketOffsets[b+1]) (half-open CSR).
type BinningGrid2D
    implements IValue, ISpatialIndex2D
{
    Bounds: Bounds2D;
    CellCounts: IntegerSize2D;
    BucketOffsets: Array<Integer>;
    ItemIndices: Array<ItemIndex>;
}

// A dense uniform binning grid over a bounded 3D region. Cells linearize
// with X varying fastest, then Y, then Z: cell (i, j, k) is bucket
// (k * CellCounts.Height + j) * CellCounts.Width + i. Same CSR encoding as
// BinningGrid2D.
type BinningGrid3D
    implements IValue, ISpatialIndex3D
{
    Bounds: Bounds3D;
    CellCounts: IntegerSize3D;
    BucketOffsets: Array<Integer>;
    ItemIndices: Array<ItemIndex>;
}

//==
// ## Space-filling curve codes

// A 2D Morton (Z-order) code (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z-order_curve):
// the bits of a cell's X and Y coordinates interleaved (X in even bit
// positions). Sorting by code groups spatially nearby cells: the basis of
// linear BVH builds and cache-friendly sweeps.
type MortonCode2D
    implements IValue, IHashable, IComparable
{
    Value: Integer;
}

// A 3D Morton (Z-order) code: X, Y, and Z coordinate bits interleaved
// (X in bit positions 0, 3, 6, ...).
type MortonCode3D
    implements IValue, IHashable, IComparable
{
    Value: Integer;
}

//==
// # Implicit surfaces
//
// Unbounded surfaces defined by an equation rather than by stored extents: the
// circular paraboloid and the general quadric that subsumes spheres, ellipsoids,
// cones, cylinders, paraboloids and hyperboloids. They are surfaces, not solids, so
// they carry no volume or containment obligation.

// An infinite circular paraboloid surface opening along Axis from Vertex
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraboloid): points at height h above the
// vertex plane lie at radius r with r * r = 4 * FocalLength * h. The reflector
// shape: rays parallel to Axis converge at the focus.
type Paraboloid
    implements IGeometry3D, IConnected, IManifold, IOrientable
{
    Vertex: Point3D;
    Axis: Direction3D;
    FocalLength: Number;
}

// A general quadric surface: the homogeneous points p with
// Transpose(p) * Coefficients * p = 0 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadric).
// Coefficients is symmetric. Spheres, ellipsoids, cones, cylinders,
// paraboloids, and hyperboloids are all special cases.
type Quadric
    implements IGeometry3D
{
    Coefficients: Matrix4x4;
}

//==
// # Kd-trees
//
// Axis-aligned binary space partitions over a copied point set: the workhorse
// index for nearest-neighbor and range queries. Node indexing and the
// leaf-order permutation array follow the conventions of the grids section.

// One node of a 2D kd-tree. SplitAxis is 0 for X, 1 for Y; internal nodes
// split space at SplitValue on that axis with children LeftChild (below)
// and RightChild (above), both node indices. Leaves have children of -1 and
// a non-empty half-open Items range into the owning tree's PointIndices.
type KdTreeNode2D
    implements IValue
{
    SplitAxis: Integer;
    SplitValue: Number;
    LeftChild: SpatialNodeIndex;
    RightChild: SpatialNodeIndex;
    Items: IntegerInterval;
}

// A kd-tree (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-d_tree) over a copy of its 2D
// point set: nearest-neighbor and range queries. Node 0 is the root;
// PointIndices is the leaf-order permutation of Points. No builder yet:
// instances come from a host that emits this encoding — see
// tracker/decisions/2026-08-04-spatial-structure-construction-in-plato.md.
type KdTree2D
    implements IValue, ISpatialIndex2D, INearestNeighbor2D
{
    Points: Array<Point2D>;
    Nodes: Array<KdTreeNode2D>;
    PointIndices: Array<ItemIndex>;
}
